Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

- Behavior area: headers, count, select, slice, search, sort, table, fmt, stats, frequency

Hard constraints:

- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Equivalence requirements:
- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.
- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: .tura/scripts/original_style_checks.py
+import csv
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+PORT = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "xsv_port.py")]
+WORK = ROOT / ".tura" / "original-style"
+
+
+def write_csv(name, rows):
+    WORK.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path = WORK / name
+    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        csv.writer(f, lineterminator="\n").writerows(rows)
+    return str(path.relative_to(ROOT))
+
+
+def run(args):
+    p = subprocess.run(PORT + args, cwd=str(ROOT), stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
+    if p.returncode != 0:
+        raise AssertionError((args, p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr))
+    return p.stdout.decode("utf-8")
+
+
+def read_out(args):
+    return list(csv.reader(run(args).splitlines()))
+
+
+def main():
+    p = write_csv("headers.csv", [["h1", "h2"], ["a", "b"]])
+    assert run(["headers", p]) == "1   h1\n2   h2\n"
+    assert run(["headers", "--just-names", p]) == "h1\nh2\n"
+    assert run(["count", p]) == "1\n"
+    assert run(["count", "--no-headers", p]) == "2\n"
+
+    p = write_csv("select.csv", [["h1", "h2", "h3"], ["a", "b", "c"]])
+    assert read_out(["select", "3-1", p]) == [["h3", "h2", "h1"], ["c", "b", "a"]]
+    assert read_out(["select", "!1-2", p]) == [["h3"], ["c"]]
+
+    p = write_csv("slice.csv", [["header"], ["a"], ["b"], ["c"], ["d"], ["e"]])
+    assert read_out(["slice", "--start", "1", "--end", "3", p]) == [["header"], ["b"], ["c"]]
+    assert read_out(["slice", "--index", "1", p]) == [["header"], ["b"]]
+
+    p = write_csv("search.csv", [["h1", "h2"], ["foobar", "barfoo"], ["a", "b"], ["barfoo", "foobar"]])
+    assert read_out(["search", "^foo", p]) == [["h1", "h2"], ["foobar", "barfoo"], ["barfoo", "foobar"]]
+    assert read_out(["search", "^foo", "--select", "h2", p]) == [["h1", "h2"], ["barfoo", "foobar"]]
+
+    p = write_csv("sort.csv", [["N", "S"], ["10", "a"], ["LETTER", "b"], ["2", "c"], ["1", "d"]])
+    assert read_out(["sort", "-N", p]) == [["N", "S"], ["LETTER", "b"], ["1", "d"], ["2", "c"], ["10", "a"]]
+
+    p = write_csv("fmt.csv", [["h1", "h2"], ["abcdef", "ghijkl"], ["mnopqr", "stuvwx"]])
+    assert run(["fmt", "--out-delimiter", "\\t", p]) == "h1\th2\nabcdef\tghijkl\nmnopqr\tstuvwx\n"
+    assert run(["fmt", "--quote-always", p]) == '"h1","h2"\n"abcdef","ghijkl"\n"mnopqr","stuvwx"\n'
+
+    p = write_csv("table.csv", [["h1", "h2", "h3"], ["abcdefg", "a", "a"], ["a", "abc", "z"]])
+    assert run(["table", p]) == "h1       h2   h3\nabcdefg  a    a\na        abc  z\n"
+
+    p = write_csv("frequency.csv", [["h1", "h2"], ["a", "x"], ["a", "y"], ["b", "y"], ["b", "z"], ["b", "z"]])
+    assert read_out(["frequency", "--limit", "1", p])[0] == ["field", "value", "count"]
+    assert read_out(["stats", "--everything", p])[0] == ["field", "type", "sum", "min", "max", "min_length", "max_length", "mean", "stddev", "median", "mode", "cardinality"]
+    print("original-style checks passed")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
*** End Patch
